# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71 (Bu-Vb Pc71)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc71
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71
**Title (English, from literature):** Not accepting legitimate correction

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 71, entitled *Sahadhammika* ("Not accepting legitimate correction"), concerns the expiation of an offense committed by a monk who makes excuses or employs ploys to evade training according to the monastic code. The introductory narrative frame involves the venerable Channa, who is depicted as refusing correction while being characterized as in training (*sikkhamāna*) [Blackstone 1995].

The rule has extensive canonical parallels across early Buddhist schools, corresponding to the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and Parivāra (Pācittiya 71), the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (Pācittiya 149), and the Prātimokṣa codes of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, and Kāśyapīya traditions in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan [Dutt 1924]. Automated text reuse analysis confirms internal Pali overlaps with the *Bhikkhupātimokkhapāḷi*, the *Parivāra* (*Katthapaññattivāra* and *Katāpattivāra*), and shared legal phrasing in adjacent Vibhaṅga rules (including Pācittiyas 2, 54, 55, 72, 75, 76, and 77), alongside cross-lingual alignment with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-3) and *Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya* (D4106-2) [DharmaNexus].
